subject: Post-call: Hosting path & residency Qs (EU primary, APAC fallback) - action plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lina Sorensen <lina.sorensen@euromedhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Hosting & residency options (EU primary) - next steps

Hi Lina — great to speak with you this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so everyone is aligned:

Summary of requirements (as I understood them)
- Primary requirement: Process and store PHI-sensitive records only within the EU (GDPR + national rules).
- APAC users: acceptable to route non-PHI traffic to APAC; any PHI must remain in EU.
- Latency SLO: <100ms p95 for European users; APAC target is less strict for now.

Options we discussed (high level)
- Hosted API (Redwood-hosted, EU regions): Fastest onboarding; supports region selection but if you require strict EU-only processing for PHI we recommend additional controls.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved EU GPU pool): Compute pinned to EU, tenant isolation, single-tenant pools — good middle ground for predictable throughput and residency.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Full control over data and keys; recommended when audit/hard residency controls are mandatory.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Please confirm whether all PHI must never leave the EU (yes/no) and whether any subset of data can be pseudonymized for APAC routing.
2) Can you loop in your security contact (name/email) and the procurement lead so we can start the SOC 2 + data flow questionnaire?
3) Marcus can run a short technical deep-dive (30–45m) to map SSO, VPC needs, and a minimal POC config. Are mornings next week (CEST) good for you?

I attached a 1‑pager that contrasts Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployment paths and an example workbook showing routing patterns. I also included a suggested POC timeline (2–4 weeks) and procurement milestones.

If helpful I can also draft the minimal scope for a Dedicated POC (EU region + key management options) so procurement sees concrete costs.

Thanks — Hannah
-- 
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0192

Attachment: redwood_hosting_options_1pager.pdf
Attachment: eu-apac-routing-examples.xlsx

From: Lina Sorensen <lina.sorensen@euromedhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Mika Tanaka <mika.tanaka@medcloud.jp>
Date: 2027-04-11T15:03:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Hosting & residency options (EU primary) - next steps

Thanks Hannah — helpful recap. Confirming the key points from our side:

- PHI must stay within the EU for all European patients. No PHI (raw identifiers or clinical notes) can be processed outside EU jurisdictions.
- Non-PHI traffic (analytics, anonymized prompts) can be routed to APAC if needed.
- Procurement timeline: we target contract signature in Q3; security review expected in May.

Two quick questions:
1) If we start with Redwood Hosted in an EU region with strict routing rules, is there an easy migration path to Dedicated or Private later without rework to the app integration?
2) For cross-region fallbacks (e.g., EU region degraded), what's Redwood's recommended approach so we don't spill PHI?

Looping in Mika (our APAC infra lead) — Mika, any constraints from the Japan site?

-Lina

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Hosting & residency options (EU primary) - next steps

Thanks for the quick confirmation, Lina — answers below. Short answers first, then proposed actions.

1) Migration path: yes — we design the API and SDK to be portable. Hosted -> Dedicated typically requires reconfiguring the endpoint and (optionally) key management; we can preserve prompt/code paths and model versions. We'll provide a migration checklist that maps network, DNS, and credentials changes.

2) Cross-region fallback guidance: if PHI cannot ever leave EU then we recommend configuring fallback policies that only use EU-hosted capacity. Options:
   - Primary: EU region (hosted or dedicated) + automatic routing that honors residency tag on requests.
   - Fallback: if EU capacity is constrained, traffic can queue/buffer or fail closed rather than spill to APAC. This is our recommended safe default for PHI.

Proposed immediate actions
- Marcus to run the technical deep-dive (30–45m) to capture SSO, network, and data flows — propose Wed/Thu next week (CEST).
- Security questionnaire + data flow diagram: I'll send the RedTeam SOC 2 packet and a minimal DF diagram template for your security team to fill.
- I will draft a Dedicated POC scope (EU region, KMS options, throughput targets) and estimated costs — we can share that doc before the deep dive.

Attached: link to the HubSpot deal and the shared Drive doc with the POC checklist.

Best — Hannah
-- 
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lina Sorensen <lina.sorensen@euromedhealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Hosting & residency options (EU primary) - next steps

Hi Lina — brief technical note from the solutions side.

If EuroMed wants a safe EU-first plan with the option to add APAC for non-PHI, here's a minimal technical config we typically recommend for the POC:
- Deployment: Dedicated EU pool (single-tenant) with private subnets. This pins compute to the EU GCP region you mentioned.
- Networking: Private Peering or VPC-SC to avoid public egress. Allowlist Redwood egress ranges for any telemetry destinations.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys (Cloud KMS or HSM) — we support wrapping model artifacts and request logs.
- Request routing: Add a residency flag in your request metadata. Our routing policy will keep PHI-tagged requests in EU and route non-PHI by best-latency.
- Fallback behavior: Configure 'fail-closed' for PHI-tagged requests and 'best-effort' for non-PHI. We can instrument tracing to surface when requests are queued/failed for auditing.

For the POC we only need a representative set of prompts (synthetic is fine), an example SSO metadata flow, and a short list of endpoints that must remain EU-only. We can draft a minimal terraform snippet to stand up the Dedicated test pool if you want.

I'll wait for Lina/Mika to propose 2–3 slots for the deep-dive and I'll include a 1‑pager that maps the Dedicated config to the procurement checklist.

Regards — Marcus
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
